experience.title: Senior Machine Learning & Data Engineer
bullets: Own full-stack and AI capabilities across Microsoft's clinical documentation products, spanning DAX Copilot and Dragon Copilot (drafting from the visit itself), Dragon Medical One (dictation and templates), PowerScribe, and the write-back into the record system.

Owned the drafting path from captured conversation to finished draft, grounded against what the record already holds so every line can be checked against a source rather than merely reading well, across health systems covering much of the country's outpatient care.

Built the review surface where the clinician edits and signs, and turned what they changed into the signal the next model is measured on - the edit is the label, so the product learns from the work rather than from a separate annotation exercise.

Extended the evaluation and release gate a version has to clear before it reaches a room, scoring drafts against what clinicians accepted and holding the whole path to HIPAA handling and ISO 27001 audit.

experience.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
bullets: Developed the in-line quality models at Stryker, reading inspection and process data so a drifting production line showed itself before it turned out implants that would fail final inspection.
Engineered image-analysis pipelines behind orthopaedic planning and device imaging, deriving the measurements downstream planning tools relied on instead of leaving them to manual annotation.
Clustered free-text device complaints and field-service reports so quality engineering saw a recurring failure mode as one problem rather than two hundred unrelated tickets.

Consolidated manufacturing, quality, service and clinical-registry sources into a single traceable data estate, which in a validated device environment is the precondition for using any of it in a model.
Produced the validation packages quality, regulatory and manufacturing engineering required, setting out what each model measured and the point at which a person had to decide instead.
